title: 17th Sitting of Second session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 under the Deputy Speaker. An urgent motion from Hussain Ziyad (Vaikaradhoo) about burnt Thilafushi waste being sent to Kanburudhoo in Haa Dhaalu was voted on and not accepted for debate (7 for, 27 against). The government's bill to amend the Utility Regulatory Authority Act (Law 26/2020), which would widen the regulator's board from 5 to 7 members and stop its chief executive voting on the board, was introduced and had its preliminary debate, with members split on party lines and several raising outer-island utility tariffs. During that debate the chair ordered Hussain Ziyad out of the chamber, and after a break at 10:32 the sitting moved to a resolution on SOE job cuts, which was still being debated when this part ends. The second half of the sitting finished the debate on a resolution by Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir about people being dismissed from government companies in the name of cutting staff, with a Baarashu member arguing against it. The chair then took two Foreign Relations Committee reports on proposed ambassadors: one for Belgium and the European Union, one non-resident ambassador to Bahrain. At voting time the resolution failed, and both ambassador nominations passed with no votes against. The sitting adjourned to 3 August 2026.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the bill and defended the government's debt handling.
Opposed the SOE resolution as baseless, saying earlier governments overstaffed state companies for internal party elections.
Presented the committee report on the Belgium and European Union nominee, covering the checks made with institutions and the committee's unanimous decision.
Presented the committee report on the Bahrain non-resident ambassador nominee, an existing ambassador to Saudi Arabia, and the committee's decision.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Moved an urgent motion that sending burnt Thilafushi waste to Kanburudhoo, which lacks a treatment system, risks health and the environment.
In the bill debate said he could not back the amendments, called them minor administrative changes, and repeated his objection to the Kanburudhoo waste site; the chair then ordered him out.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Backed the bill as a way to oversee water, power and waste services under one regulator, and defended the government's record.
Argued the regulator needs more powers and a budget to monitor providers, and that the ministry should not bypass it.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: On the bill said it has only a few main amendments and the regulator has so far failed on affordability, citing higher atoll business tariffs and Stelco profits.
On the SOE resolution said it is a real issue, pointing to a Finance Ministry circular telling state companies to cut 33 percent of staff.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Argued the resolution is political: said the previous MDP government also dismissed people for political reasons and that PNC-era company hiring grew, while right-sizing is needed to fix company finances.
On the Bahrain report, supported it, saying the nominee has foreign-service experience and that the nominations fit the government's cost-cutting aims.

speakers.name: Hassan Waheed
positions: Presented the government bill: it tightens how the Utility Regulatory Authority is run, widens its board from 5 to 7 with technical members, and removes the chief executive's board vote.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill, saying the chief executive having no board vote and more technical members add checks and balances.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Welcomed the bill but said the regulator's board change works only if it is given full powers and a monitoring budget, and the ministry stays out of its role.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supported the bill and said the regulator must monitor island service providers, citing power cuts and past water and sewerage contracts in Addu.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill and said the Majlis should look into past outer-island utility projects, alleging an overpriced Dhidhdhoo powerhouse that was not finished.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Opposed the bill as drafted, calling the changes minor and saying they do not fix real problems such as the tariff gap between Malé and the atolls; wants changes at committee.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill as an administrative fix and rejected opposition criticism, saying the amendments aim to speed up services.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the bill, saying its main aim is bringing basic island services under one system faster, and criticised past contracts.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: On the SOE resolution said the state cannot spend most of its revenue on salaries and still run projects, so staff costs must be cut.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Backed the SOE resolution, saying the 33 percent cut harms families and that PNC members were pushed to vote as the President's office directs (speech continues in the next part).

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the Belgium/EU report, saying there was little to add as the nominee is highly capable.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: On the Bahrain report, questioned the cost and benefit of embassies abroad, especially in Europe, given the exchange rate; said he had no objection to the nominee.

decisions: The urgent motion on Thilafushi waste going to Kanburudhoo was not accepted for debate (7 for, 27 against, 0 abstaining; 18 needed).
The Utility Regulatory Authority Act (Law 26/2020) amendment bill had its first reading and a preliminary debate.
The uninhabited islands and lagoons lease bill was introduced for first reading.
The resolution to halt the Permanent Residency Programme was introduced for first reading.
The chair ordered Hussain Ziyad (Vaikaradhoo) out of the chamber during the bill debate.
Debate on the SOE job-cuts resolution continued and was not finished in this part.
Debate on the resolution on political dismissals from government companies was closed and it went to a vote.
The resolution on political dismissals did not pass, with 6 yes and 45 no.
Fathimath Diyana's appointment as ambassador to Belgium and the European Union was approved 52-0.
Ahmed Sareer's appointment as non-resident ambassador to Bahrain was approved 53-0.
The sitting was adjourned to Monday 3 August 2026 at 9:00.
